A popular market narrative attributes much of that move to fiscal deficits. According to analysis from BNP Paribas, the evidence so far points in the opposite direction: budget concerns have played almost no meaningful role, the investment firm noted.

That may be about to change, the bank said. Deficit arithmetic is poised to draw far more attention and help power the next leg higher in yields. Three developments are converging. Federal Reserve rate increases are lifting the government’s interest burden. Recent deficit readings have deteriorated. Midterm elections are also approaching, raising the political profile of fiscal outcomes.

If those concerns re-enter market discussion, BNP Paribas argued, term premiums on longer-dated bonds could expand and become the fresh catalyst for higher long-end rates. Until now, other forces have dominated the backup in yields. In the months ahead, however, the combination of a heavier interest bill, weaker deficit prints, and the electoral calendar could shift the conversation and leave fiscal sustainability as a more visible driver of the Treasury curve.
